gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns failure to establish that perturbed trajectories remain in the domain K required by finite-horizon tracking. ISSUE-001 concerns endpoint stationarity of certificate axioms, not the trajectory-domain hypothesis or uniform-continuity application.

The gold issue is the unhandled equality case 4||a_t||²−δ=0 in the rank-1 approximation boundary-inward proof. ISSUE-001 identifies a different endpoint degeneracy in the scalar/factorization certificate remainder and does not diagnose this equality-case proof step.

The gold issue is overclaiming asymptotic unboundedness from finite T=600 experiments. ISSUE-002 concerns an internal contradiction between two numerical pass-region reports at eta=0.6 and does not address the asymptotic inference from finite trajectories.

Both identify that the closed threshold endpoint δ=η is included in the stationarity/equality claim even though the certificate remainder vanishes at nonstationary boundary points, so the endpoint uniqueness/stationarity assertion is unsupported.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The endpoint δ=δ_th(η)=η admits nonstationary certificate-boundary points with zero one-step certificate change, invalidating the claimed equality-only-at-stationary-points condition and the closed-endpoint uniqueness claim.

component_coverage.gold_component: At the threshold endpoint, nonstationary boundary points can have zero certificate change, so stationarity/equality and the corresponding closed-endpoint uniqueness claim fail.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies the endpoint inclusion, zero remainder at δ=η, nonstationary boundary examples, and that stationarity holds only on the open interval.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue is missing coverage of every arbitrary nonterminal level by an unbalanced global minimizer before applying local uniqueness. ISSUE-001 addresses an endpoint stationarity axiom and does not recognize the level-coverage premise.

The gold issue is nonuniqueness under increasing reparameterization of the state coordinate. ISSUE-001 concerns restricting an endpoint stationarity axiom and does not diagnose coordinate reparameterization freedom.

The gold issue concerns the approximation remark's incorrect use of q_{η'}(δ_t)≤0 instead of the strict condition q_{η'}(δ_t)<0 for interior mapping. ISSUE-001 discusses a different endpoint δ=η stationarity failure and does not identify the q=0 approximation-step counterexample.
